claim.text: BREAKING: Harwick council just slashed library funding by 40%. Eastgate and Millrow branches will close by spring. Shameful. #SaveHarwickLibraries

sources.title: City of Harwick - Regular Council Meeting Minutes (approved), Item 7: FY27 budget items
sources.text: 7a. Stormwater utility fee schedule. Staff presented the revised fee schedule for residential parcels. Councillor Pardo asked whether the senior discount would continue; staff confirmed it would. Received and filed. 7b. FY27 Draft Operating Budget. The Finance Director summarised the projected shortfall and the list of reductions proposed by departments. Motion (Obi / Chen) to reduce the Library Services line by 40 percent and to direct the City Manager to close the Eastgate and Millrow branches by 31 March. Discussion: Councillor Lindqvist said the motion 'guts a service people actually use'; Councillor Obi said the city 'cannot keep funding three buildings within a mile of each other'. Motion FAILED 3-6. Substitute motion (Lindqvist / Adeyemi) to reduce the Library Services line by 12 percent and direct staff to return with a study of options for the Eastgate and Millrow branches, including consolidation, shared use with the recreation department, or reduced hours. Substitute motion CARRIED 6-3. The Clerk noted that under Council Rule 14 any closure of a public facility requires a separate ordinance with two readings. 7c. Parking enforcement contract renewal. Deferred to the next meeting at the request of staff.

sources.headline: Council trims library budget after heated debate
sources.text: After nearly two hours of public comment, Harwick City Council on Tuesday approved a 12 percent reduction to library funding in the draft budget, rejecting a deeper 40 percent cut proposed by Councillor Obi. The approved motion asks staff to study the future of the Eastgate and Millrow branches, but no closures were voted on. 'A 12 percent cut will be felt - in hours, in staffing, in programs,' said Priya Nandakumar, president of the library workers' local. The budget returns for final adoption next month.

We have seen posts saying that Eastgate and Millrow will close. That is not correct. Council has asked staff to study options for those two branches and to report back. No branch is closing at this time, and all branches keep their current hours through the end of the fiscal year. We encourage residents to take part in the upcoming listening sessions.

state.desk_note: Reader tip line, ticket TIP-20931. Assigned: local desk. Minutes confirmed as the approved version on the city site.

article.headline: Pellham Man Sworn In As Mayor After Winning Office Fantasy League
article.body: PELLHAM - Clutching a plastic trophy and a laminated certificate printed at the library, claims adjuster Doug Harnett was sworn in Monday as mayor of Pellham after finishing first in his office's fantasy football league. 'The bylaws were clear,' said Harnett, pointing to an old group-chat message that read 'winner gets to be mayor lol'. City clerk staff reportedly watched the ceremony from the lobby 'out of professional curiosity.' Harnett's first act was renaming the budget committee 'the waiver wire.'
article.footer: More from the Gazette: 'Local Dog Elected To Zoning Board, Immediately Recuses Self From Fire Hydrant Vote'

HEADLINE: Coffee Reverses Aging, Scientists Confirm

SUBHEAD: Your morning cup could be the fountain of youth

BODY: Researchers at the Brannock Institute for Metabolic Research report that elderly mice given high doses of trigonelline, a compound found in roasted coffee beans, showed improved grip strength and longer running times compared with untreated mice over an eight-week study. The team also observed higher levels of a cellular energy molecule in muscle tissue. The study involved 24 mice and was published this week in a peer-reviewed journal. The authors caution that the dose used was far higher than anything a person could get from drinking coffee and that no human trials have been done. 'We would not suggest anyone change their coffee habits based on this,' said lead author Dr. Ines Farrow. 'This is an early step in understanding one pathway.' An independent researcher not involved in the study said the result was 'interesting but a long way from the clinic.'

consistency.instructions: How does the HEADLINE relate to the BODY?

criteria.consistent: The headline fairly summarises the body
criteria.overstated: The headline claims more certainty or scope than the body supports
criteria.understated: The headline plays down what the body reports
criteria.contradicts_body: The headline asserts something the body says is false

human_evidence.instructions: Does the BODY report any results in humans?

exaggeration.instructions: How far does the HEADLINE go beyond the BODY?

criteria.definition: The headline matches the body
A minor simplification that loses no key qualifier
It drops an important qualifier such as species or dose
It presents a preliminary animal finding as an established human fact
It asserts something the body explicitly contradicts

subhead_overreach.instructions: Does the SUBHEAD make a claim that the BODY does not support?

consistency.note: A 24-mouse study with an unreachable dose becomes 'reverses aging, scientists confirm'; the author's 'would not suggest anyone change their habits' pushes some reviewers to 'contradicts'.

exaggeration.note: The headline turns an early mouse result into a confirmed human fact (level 3); since the body says the dose is unreachable and the author disclaims behavioural advice, many would call it a contradiction (level 4).

subhead_overreach.note: 'could be the fountain of youth' is hedged with 'could', but it still ties a morning cup to anti-aging when the body says a person can't reach the dose; reviewers split on whether a hedged tease counts as a claim.

claim.speaker: Rowan Tess, candidate for premier (fictional), speaking at a Northgate rally
claim.text: Under this government, unemployment in this province has doubled. Doubled! Ask anyone looking for work.
claim.video_context: The line came about twelve minutes into a forty-minute speech that also covered hospital wait lists, a promised ferry link and fuel taxes. The crowd of roughly three hundred, mostly local, cheered the line. Tess did not refer to young people or to any particular region in the minutes before or after it.

stat_release.text: Highlights. The provincial unemployment rate was essentially unchanged from the same quarter a year earlier. Employment grew in health care, construction and public administration and fell slightly in retail trade. The participation rate edged down, reflecting an ageing population. Youth unemployment (ages 15-24) rose over the year, driven mainly by fewer summer hires in accommodation and food services. Regional detail: the survey's regional breakdown groups the province into four economic regions; the Northgate area is included in the North economic region, for which the rate was also essentially unchanged. Long-term trend: the provincial rate remains lower than it was at the start of the current government's term. Technical note: estimates are subject to sampling variability; month-to-month changes in small regions should be interpreted with caution. Seasonally adjusted and unadjusted series are both available in the data tables. The next release is scheduled for the third quarter. Revisions: the first-quarter estimates were revised slightly upward following the annual benchmark to population estimates; the revision did not change the direction of any trend described above.

state.campaign_response: Asked about the figure, a Tess campaign spokesperson said the candidate 'was clearly talking about youth unemployment in Northgate, which everyone in that room is living with.' The spokesperson did not provide a source for a doubling.
state.reporter_note: We asked the statistics office for Northgate-only youth figures. The office said it does not publish youth unemployment below the economic-region level. We also asked the office whether any provincial series had doubled over the government's term; a spokesperson said none of the headline labour series had.
state.archive_note: Our desk rated a similar Tess claim last spring ('unemployment is up by half') as Mostly False after the campaign said it referred to a single town's plant closure. The campaign did not correct that claim on its website, and the line reappeared in two later speeches. Our standards editor asked that this check note the pattern but rate the new claim on its own evidence, as our guidelines require. A spokesperson for the governing party, contacted separately, called the doubling claim 'invented' and pointed to the long-term trend in the release; we do not rely on partisan statements for the rating.

verdict.instructions: How does `stat_release` bear on `claim.text` as spoken?

claim_population.instructions: Which population does `claim.text`, as spoken, refer to?

narrowed.instructions: Does `campaign_response` narrow the claim to a different population than the one named in `claim.text`?

northgate_youth_data.instructions: Does the state contain a published youth unemployment figure for Northgate specifically?

rating.instructions: How should `claim.text`, as spoken, be rated?

criteria.definition: Matches the evidence in substance and detail
Right in substance, minor detail missing
Accurate and inaccurate elements in roughly equal measure
A kernel of truth, but the main thrust is wrong
Contradicted by the evidence
Contradicted, with no factual basis at all

verdict.note: The claim is about provincial unemployment, which the release says is essentially unchanged and lower than at the start of the term; only youth unemployment rose, which a few would treat as a mixed kernel.

claim_population.note: 'unemployment in this province', and video_context says Tess mentioned neither youth nor a region around the line.

narrowed.note: The claim says 'unemployment in this province'; the spokesperson reframes it as youth unemployment in Northgate, a narrower population and area.

northgate_youth_data.note: The reporter note says the office does not publish youth figures below the region level; Northgate sits inside the North region.

rating.note: As spoken the claim is contradicted by the provincial figures and the office says no headline series doubled (level 4); the rise in youth unemployment gives it a kernel of truth (level 3).

rating_policy.R1: A claim may be rated True or False only when the evidence includes at least two independent sources that address it.
rating_policy.R2: Exception to R1: a single primary official record (for example a court filing, a statute, certified election results, or signed minutes of a public body) is sufficient on its own.
rating_policy.R3: Anonymous or unattributable sources never count toward R1 or R2.
rating_policy.R4: If neither R1 nor R2 is met, rate Unverifiable.

HEADLINE: Minor Leak Reported at Dorrow Chemical Plant

BODY: A chlorine leak at the Dorrow Chemical plant on the city's east side sent three workers to hospital on Wednesday and prompted authorities to order residents within two kilometres to shelter indoors for most of the afternoon. Fire crews contained the leak at a storage valve about four hours after it began. article.headline: Marlowe Bay desalination plant clears final hurdle
article.body: The Marlowe Bay desalination plant cleared its last regulatory hurdle on Thursday when the regional water board approved its intake permit, ending a four-year review. The plant, which will cost $148 million to build, is designed to supply about a fifth of the peninsula's drinking water in dry years. Supporters on the water board said the plant would reduce the region's reliance on the Tanner Aquifer, which has dropped to record lows twice in the past decade. Opponents, including the Marlowe Bay Fishers' Cooperative, argued that the intake screens would harm larval fish and that the brine outflow had not been studied enough near the eelgrass beds. The permit requires the operator to fund an independent marine monitoring program for ten years and to cut intake flows during spawning season. Construction is expected to begin next spring. The operator, Peninsula Water Partners (fictional), said customer bills would rise by an amount it has not yet disclosed; the utility commission will review any rate change separately. Board member Liesel Okafor, who voted no, said she was 'not convinced the alternatives were taken seriously', pointing to a recycled-water proposal the board rejected last year. The cooperative's president, Arne Duval, said the group was reviewing its legal options but had not decided whether to challenge the permit. A spokesperson for the county said the plant's power supply would come partly from a solar array to be built on the former landfill site, which still needs its own planning approval. Local business groups welcomed the decision, citing the risk of water restrictions for restaurants and hotels during drought summers.

Voters are told to stay away and threatened or intimidated

verdict.note: St. Brendan's is locked, a grain of truth, but the notice and live blog show it moved two blocks away, the other Ward 7 stations are open, and Sec. 12-4 says a relocation does not close the precinct; the 'shut down to stop us voting' thrust is false.

law_condition_met.note: A burst water main making the hall unusable fits 'an emergency that renders the designated location unusable'; the notice doesn't use the word 'unusable', hence the residual.

harm.note: 'Don't bother going' tells voters of a functioning (relocated) precinct not to vote, and the hotline shows callers assuming voting was cancelled, which is level 3; there's no threat, so the top level gets little mass.

viral_post.text: New study PROVES the Vexlo nasal spray causes heart inflammation in teens. 1 in 50 kids affected! Link below. They don't want you to see this.

preprint_record.title: Myocarditis signals after intranasal Vexlo administration in adolescents: a pharmacovigilance analysis
preprint_record.server_policy: Preprints are not peer reviewed. Withdrawn preprints remain visible with a notice; the original text is retained for the record.
preprint_record.abstract: Background: Vexlo is an intranasal decongestant licensed for ages 12 and over. We examined spontaneous adverse event reports mentioning Vexlo and myocarditis. Methods: We searched a national spontaneous reporting database for reports in adolescents aged 12 to 17 and calculated reporting odds ratios against all other nasal decongestants. Results: We identified reports suggesting a disproportionality signal. Limitations: spontaneous reports cannot establish incidence or causation; reporting may be stimulated by media coverage; duplicate reports are possible. Conclusions: Further study is warranted.
preprint_record.withdrawal_notice: The authors have withdrawn this manuscript. After posting, the authors identified a coding error that counted each follow-up report as a new case, inflating the number of cases approximately fifteen-fold. After correction, no disproportionality signal remains. The authors do not wish this work to be cited.

state.regulator_statement: The medicines agency (fictional) reviewed Vexlo's safety data after media interest and found no evidence of an increased risk of myocarditis. Product information is unchanged. Patients with concerns should speak to a pharmacist.

news_coverage.text: Before its withdrawal, the preprint was picked up by several wellness sites, one of which added the '1 in 50' figure without citing a source. Pharmacists in two regions said they had fielded questions from parents asking whether to stop using the spray. The lead author told us the team withdrew the paper within a week of posting once they found the coding error, and that they were 'dismayed' it was still being shared. An independent pharmacoepidemiologist said disproportionality analyses are hypothesis-generating tools and are never designed to estimate how many users are affected.

comment_thread: lol the preprint literally says WITHDRAWN at the top
my cousin's kid used it and was fine but still, scary
1 in 50 where does that number even come from
the abstract itself says it can't show causation??
state.pharmacist_association_note: The national pharmacists' association said it had issued a short advice sheet for members after the posts spread. The sheet says the preprint has been withdrawn, that the regulator found no increased risk, and that parents should not stop any medicine without advice. It also reminds pharmacists that decongestant sprays should not be used for more than a week at a time, a long-standing label warning unrelated to the myocarditis question.

criteria.definition: Matches the evidence in substance and detail
Right in substance, minor detail wrong
Accurate and inaccurate elements in roughly equal measure
A kernel of truth, but the main thrust is wrong
Contradicted by the evidence

claim_status.note: Banner WITHDRAWN plus the withdrawal notice.

figure_origin.note: The coverage says a wellness site 'added the 1 in 50 figure without citing a source'; the abstract gives no rate, and disproportionality analyses can't estimate one.

proves_causation.note: The abstract's own limitations say spontaneous reports 'cannot establish incidence or causation', and it concludes 'further study is warranted'.

rating.note: The post presents a withdrawn preprint, whose signal vanished after correction, as proof, with an invented rate; that is the top level. Some would stop at 'contradicted' since the preprint was real, not fabricated.

verdict.note: Production does end and about 600 roles are affected (register agrees), but the site becomes a distribution centre and roles are offered, so 'close' and 'jobs lost' are only partly right; union framing lets some reviewers call it supported.

plant_closes.note: The company says the plant will be converted to a distribution centre.

framing_fairness.note: The union says production at Oakfield ends and few will relocate, while the company and register frame it as conversion with offered roles; the headline is contested rather than plainly misleading.

jobs_lost_fair.note: Every worker is offered a role, so no one's job is formally eliminated, but the union says a 90-minute move means most won't take it and the register records a mass layoff; reviewers split evenly.

state.text: Journalist? The Maplecroft county jail is hiding a death in custody from last weekend. Guy in cell block C. They're calling it a transfer.
Thanks for reaching out. Can you tell me how you know this? Do you work there or know someone who does? Any name, date, document?
can't say how I know. people talk. just check it
Understood. I'll make some calls. Is there a way to reach you again?
no. don't try to find me

Called Maplecroft Sheriff's Office PIO - 'no comment on individual detainees'. Checked county medical examiner's public case list: no case listed with Maplecroft jail as place of death this month. The state jail-death reporting portal updates quarterly; last update was before the alleged date.

verdict.instructions: Based on the conversation and the reporter's note, how should the tipster's claim be rated at this point?

criteria.definition: Nothing checkable
A facility is named
A facility and a rough time
Place, time and an identifying detail about the person or incident

verdict.note: The tip is anonymous and unsourced; the ME list shows nothing, but the portal is not yet updated and the PIO only declined to comment, so nothing settles it.

tipster_access.note: 'can't say how I know' is a refusal, but 'people talk' hints at hearsay; reviewers split between the two.

me_list_rules_out.note: An absence from the ME's public list is evidence against, but the note doesn't say every jail death appears there promptly, so it doesn't rule the death out.

detail_level.note: Maplecroft jail, 'last weekend' and 'cell block C' plus the 'transfer' cover story give place, time and an identifying detail, though some would say block C doesn't identify the person.

fidelity.note: 'goes too far and too fast' vs 'goes too far, too fast' is a trivial change, and her motion is to hold the item until the flood study, matching 'delayed until the flood study is finished'.
